A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same work, renamed from DCE to EDC. Common methods, tables and figures can be matched reliably. However, v2 references supplementary material that its PDF does not contain, whereas v3 includes Appendices A-E, limiting comparison of previously undocumented implementation details.

before.justification: v2 reports original human evaluations, downstream model-training results and caption comparisons in Tables 2-5 and Figures 1-2 and 6.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and reports additional caption-method comparisons, corpus analyses and detailed MMBench results.

M1.justification: The specialist-based pipeline and both prompt templates are retained. Section 3.3 changes the region-captioning model specification from Qwen-72B to Qwen2-72B-AWQ, which v2 already specified for image captioning. Newly documented API use and relation-selection rules do not establish when implementation changed; correction, clarification and actual component changes cannot be reliably distinguished.

E1.justification: The downstream benchmarks and COCO-118K coverage are retained. However, both versions' Section 3.4 attributes the 1M images to DenseFusion, while v3 Appendix B describes sampling them from LAION. The supplied PDFs do not establish whether these describe the same images or a changed training corpus.

E2.justification: New Table 3 substantially expands caption-method comparisons with DenseFusion, DCI, DOCCI, IT and ReCap across the two backbones, alongside ShareGPT4V. ReCap also joins the main benchmark comparisons in Tables 4-5. The earlier human, InternVL2 and LLaVA-NeXT annotation comparisons remain in Table 6.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces measurement procedures for new caption analyses: Vicuna-v1.5 tokenized average length and per-sentence lexical frequencies. Section 4.1 retains the existing downstream experimental setup. Table 9 newly discloses training budgets and hyperparameters rather than establishing revisions to those experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices B, D and E substantially expand the available analyses with caption-length comparisons, lexical composition, word clouds, reasoning/perception breakdowns on MMBench and four additional caption case studies. The earlier annotation comparison and aircraft/honey examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The added corpus averages characterize captions rather than estimate experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial comparator and diagnostic results in Tables 3, 8 and 10 and the appendix figures. The retained LLaVA-NeXT OKVQA baseline changes from 44.3 to 54.3, while the authors' 57.2 remains unchanged. The authors' other main benchmark scores and the original 118K annotation-comparison scores are retained.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, mathematical derivations or proofs. The added appendix material explains implementation and empirical analyses rather than introducing mathematical theory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that combining visual-specialist attributes and relations through LLM caption fusion improves multimodal understanding and reasoning. The 1M-plus-118K annotation contribution and two-backbone validation remain. Renaming and rewritten abstract/conclusion language do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explains selecting a dominant relative relation to reduce redundancy, motivates API use through recognition limitations, and interprets the new lexical and capability analyses. Existing limitations concerning OCR thresholds, absent Chinese training captions and detector noise remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C and Tables 7 and 9 supply previously unavailable specialist identities, API dependencies, relation-selection details, optimizer settings, learning rates, batch sizes and epochs. The original prompt templates are relocated unchanged. Conversely, v2's repository URL and explicit dataset-release promise disappear, although a future source-code release remains promised.

R1.justification: v3 adds DCI, DOCCI, specialist-model references and supporting captioning literature. Section 2 replaces the specific DenseFusion/GPT-4V cost contrast with broader discussion of hallucination and factual accuracy. The central positioning of visual specialists against human and generalist-LMM captioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related-work discussion are extensively rewritten; related work gains numbered subsections, and a dedicated comparison section is introduced. Prompt listings move into organized appendices with expanded explanations. The title, method name and author/affiliation text also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds the caption-method comparison table, four appendix tables, a lexical chart, word clouds and additional illustrated cases. It relocates and reformats existing displays: v2's prompt Figures 4-5 become appendix Figures 5-6, while its case-study Figure 6 becomes Figure 4.

improvement.justification: The added specialist and training documentation and direct caption-method comparisons make v3 more reproducible and easier to assess. Caption and capability analyses also strengthen the available evidence. These gains are qualified by unresolved open-source-only claims versus disclosed Baidu API use, unclear 1M-image provenance and removal of the repository pointer, supporting a limited overall improvement.
